(Summit, Mississippi) | college = * [[Florida Atlantic Owls men's basketball|Florida Atlantic]] (2020–2024) * [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]] (2024–2025) | highlights = * [[List of NCAA Division I men's basketball champions|NCAA champion]] ([[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2025]]) * First-team All-[[Conference USA|C-USA]] (2023) * Second-team All-[[American Athletic Conference|AAC]] (2024) * Third-team All-C-USA (2022) * [[Conference USA men's basketball tournament|C-USA tournament]] MVP ([[2023 Conference USA men's basketball tournament|2023]]) }} '''Alijah Martin''' (born December 26, 2001) is an American [[college basketball]] player for the [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida Gators]] of the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC). He previously played for the [[Florida Atlantic Owls men's basketball|Florida Atlantic Owls]]. == Career == Martin attended [[North Pike School District|North Pike High School]] in [[Summit, Mississippi]].{{Cite web |last=Magazine |first=The Ballers |date=2024-07-31 |title=Alijah Martin: College Basketball Player, University of Florida |url=https://www.theballersmagazine.com/post/alijah-martin-college-basketball-player-university-of-florida-full-interview |access-date=2025-04-08 |website=The Ballers Magazine |language=en}} A multi-sport athlete, he played [[American football|football]] as a [[quarterback]], passing for 2,100 yards and rushing for 1,300 yards in his senior season.{{Cite web |last=Brockway |first=Kevin |title=Grad transfer guard Alijah Martin explains why he left FAU for Florida basketball |url=https://www.gainesville.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2024/09/26/florida-basketball-guard-alijah-martin-on-why-he-left-fau-for-uf/75304552007/ |access-date=2025-03-24 |website=Gainesville Sun |language=en-US}} In his senior basketball season, he averaged 25.4 points, 8.7 rebounds, and 3.4 steals per game, before committing to play college basketball at [[Florida Atlantic University]].{{Cite web |title=North Pike’s Alijah Martin verbally commits to FAU |url=https://www.wjtv.com/sports/friday-night-rewind/north-pikes-alijah-martin-verbally-commits-to-fau/ |website=WJTV}} After playing sparingly as a freshman for the Owls, he averaged 13.9 points and 5.3 rebounds per game as a sophomore, being named to the all-conference third team.{{Cite web |last=Wallace |first=Eric J. |title=5 things to know about Florida Atlantic basketball star sophomore Alijah Martin |url=https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/sports/college/2023/03/21/alijah-martin-5-things-about-florida-atlantic-basketball-star-march-madness-fau/70034019007/ |access-date=2025-03-24 |website=The Palm Beach Post |language=en-US}} The following season, he averaged 13.4 points and 5.3 rebounds per game, helping lead Florida Atlantic to the school's first ever Final Four appearance.{{Cite web |last=Weinberger |first=Zach |title=Johnell Davis joins Alijah Martin: Declare for 2023 NBA Draft but preserve college eligibility |url=https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/sports/college/owls/2023/04/09/faus-alijah-martin-declares-for-nba-draft-but-could-still-return-to-owls/70097765007/ |access-date=2025-03-24 |website=The Palm Beach Post |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |date=2023-04-10 |title=Alijah Martin declares for NBA Draft, but it may not be end of his college career |url=https://www.wptv.com/sports/college-sports/florida-atlantic-university/alijah-martin-declares-for-nba-draft-but-it-may-not-be-end-of-his-college-career |access-date=2025-03-24 |website=WPTV News Channel 5 West Palm |language=en}} In his final season with the Owls, he averaged 13.1 points, 5.9 rebounds and 1.6 assists per game, before entering the [[NCAA transfer portal|transfer portal]].{{Cite web |last=Pugliese |first=Nick |title=Alijah Martin joins exodus of Florida Atlantic basketball players entering transfer portal |url=https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2024/04/06/alijah-martin-joins-exodus-of-florida-atlantic-owls-entering-transfer-portal/73230768007/ |access-date=2025-03-24 |website=The Palm Beach Post |language=en-US}} In April 2024, Martin announced his decision to transfer to the [[University of Florida]].{{Cite web |date=2024-04-21 |title=Final Four star Martin going from FAU to Florida |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/39987927/alijah-martin-part-fau-final-four-run-joining-florida |access-date=2025-03-24 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2024-04-22 |title=Former FAU standout Alijah Martin signs with Florida over Alabama, Arkansas, Michigan and others |url=https://apnews.com/article/alijah-martin-florida-fau-a196e04b87c4abdc871b21321eba5eda |access-date=2025-03-24 |website=AP News |language=en}} He made an instant impact, emerging as the Gators' starting shooting guard.{{Cite web |last=Brockway |first=Kevin |title=How Alijah Martin's NCAA Tournament experience could help Florida basketball in March Madness |url=https://www.gainesville.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2025/03/20/florida-basketball-guard-alijah-martin-adds-postseason-pedigree-to-uf-roster/82543588007/ |access-date=2025-03-24 |website=Gainesville Sun |language=en-US}} In a game against [[Southern Illinois Salukis men's basketball|Southern Illinois]], he recorded 32 points, nine rebounds, and five assists, leading Florida to a 93–68 victory.{{Cite web |date=2024-11-23 |title=FAU transfer Alijah Martin sees Final Four potential in unbeaten Gators |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/2024/11/22/florida-gators-basketball-fau-transfer-alijah-martin-todd-golden/ |access-date=2025-03-24 |website=Orlando Sentinel |language=en-US}} Against [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]] in the [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|Final Four]], he scored 17 points in a 79–73 victory.{{Cite web |title=Florida's Martin gets second chance at a championship |url=https://baynews9.com/fl/tampa/sports/2025/04/07/florida-gators--houston-cougars--final-four--college-basketball--alijah-martin |access-date=2025-04-08 |website=baynews9.com |language=en}} In the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|National Championship Game]] against [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston]], he tallied seven points, helping lead the Gators to the school's third national championship.{{Cite news |last=Schnell |first=Lindsay |date=2025-04-08 |title=Florida’s Alijah Martin will talk about his second chance at the Final Four forever |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6263464/2025/04/08/florida-basketball-alijah-martin-fau-ncaa-title/ |access-date=2025-04-08 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}
